title: Great Day recording, Andy Secrist and Mildred Bailey
summary: He arranged Youmans songs for Whiteman on the coast; Bix was absent, Mildred Bailey sang, and Whiteman wanted the Great Day record recalled.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Well, the band had gone out on the coast and they had been out there for a long time. I had made -- I was so

taken with the tunes that he had: Without a Song, Great Day, "Happy Because I'm In Love and there's another one. Anyway I made them all, sent them out, and they recorded-- Bing recorded More Than You Know." Bing recorded Without a Song and they didn't record Happy Because I'm in Love, but "Great Day," at that time Bix wasn't in the band. He had been sick and he didn't play the chorus on "Great Day." I mention this for a reason. He didn't play it. I didn't like what Andy did.

Andy Secrist played it, and Bix, I know what Bix would have done. It would have been tasty, whatever it was. Andy, I think, smeared all over the thing, but Bing did a great job on it, "Without A Song" (Mildred Bailey -- ed.) Mildred had just come into the band. Bing had brought around Mildred who was Rinker's sister and she had just come into the band. I guess she didn't have anything to do, any songs arranged for her.

So this was her -- she did More Than You Know, and from what I hear -- I never heard it done, they didn't record it -- from what I hear, she did it very well and Paul was crazy about it. But anyway later on after "Great Day" came out, I had told Vince that I was going to send it to Paul and when he heard Great Day he thought Ferde did it. I don't know why. Ferde would have done a fine job, but he said to me, that arrangement that Ferde did -- Ferde hadn't done it

at all, and I guess maybe he was trying to spare my feelings. He said, 'that stinks. That's lousy,' and he said, 'I am going to get it recalled.' You know, he went up to the Columbia office and tried to get them to bring that back if anything is possible to -- you know, not to put it out. And to recall it.
